findings.trigger: Fresh installation without <config dir>/mech/evolution.json -> EvolutionConfigService resolves its path as get_config_dir()/mech/evolution.json only and never asks resolve_mech_file(), so the shipped services/mech/defaults/evolution.json (which mech_defaults.py lines 12-20 promise is used) is ignored and _get_fallback_config() is used instead. The fallback has exactly one community tier (MEDIUM 26-50, multiplier 1.0) and no MASSIVE tier, so get_community_size_info() returns multiplier 1.0 for every member count and the logarithmic scaling at line 210-213 can never run; calculate_dynamic_cost() therefore ignores community size on every installation that has not written its own evolution.json. Also: the fallback comment says it 'matches evolution_config.json', a file name that does not exist in this section, so the two copies (fallback dict vs. shipped file) have no mechanism keeping them in step.
findings.suggestion: Resolve the default path through resolve_mech_file('evolution.json') like decay.json (mech_evolutions.py:355), and let the hard-coded fallback be the last resort only. If a test pins the two copies together (fallback dict == shipped file), the drift becomes visible.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see services/mech/defaults/ - whether an evolution.json is shipped there and whether it differs from _get_fallback_config(). If they are identical the effect is only the missing MASSIVE tier, which may be intended for the fallback.

findings.trigger: decay.json gives a level a decay that differs from the evolution config's 'decay_per_day' (e.g. level 5 -> 50 cents in decay.json, 1.0 in evolution.json / the fallback, which has 1.0 for every level 1-10) -> get_evolution_level_info(5).decay_per_day returns 0.5 (it overrides from decay.json, lines 350-365) while get_all_evolution_levels()[5].decay_per_day returns 1.0 (it reads only the evolution config). Two public functions of the same module answer the same question differently; whichever table/overview is built from get_all_evolution_levels shows a decay the mech does not actually have, while the single-level path and the real decay (progress_service via decay.json) say otherwise.
findings.suggestion: Build get_all_evolution_levels() from get_evolution_level_info() per level, or factor the decay.json lookup into one helper both use.
findings.unsure_why: Callers of get_all_evolution_levels are outside this section; if nothing displays its decay_per_day the drift has no visible effect.

findings.trigger: get_evolution_level_info(core_data['level']) returns None (level key missing from the operator's base_evolution_costs) or raises (malformed entry -> AttributeError/TypeError) -> _calculate_decay_data returns decay_rate=1.0, is_immortal=False as a 'default fallback' (lines 675, 690-701). get_decay_info() then computes survival_hours = power / (1/24) and get_projections() reports hours_until_zero and a survival_category of 'critical'/'urgent'/... - numbers nobody measured, presented with success=True. For a level-11 mech (real decay 0.0, immortal) this announces a death that never comes; for any other level it reports the wrong remaining time. The same file replaced exactly this pattern for progress data with None (review C24, lines 719-727) but left decay on 1.0.
findings.suggestion: Return decay_rate=None / is_immortal=None when the level info is unavailable, propagate None into survival_hours and hours_until_zero, and let get_projections report 'unknown' instead of a category; or return success=False.
findings.unsure_why: The failure is logged at ERROR, so it is not fully silent; how often get_evolution_level_info returns None for the current level in practice depends on config files I cannot see.

findings.trigger: One MechDataResult is built from three independent state reads: core_data['level'/'power'] from mech_service.get_mech_state_service (line 539), prog_state.level/evo_max/evo_current from progress_service.get_state() (line 569), and a third get_state() for the 'bars' field (line 888). A donation or level-up landing between the reads (or a decay tick crossing 0 between them) yields a result whose current_level, decay_rate and speed (all from core_data['level']) belong to level N while level_name, next_level, next_threshold and amount_needed (from prog_state) belong to level N+1 - reported with success=True and then cached for 10 s. If mech_service derives its level from total donations (the very thing line 634-635 of this file calls 'wrong with dynamic costs'), the disagreement is permanent rather than a race.
findings.suggestion: Read the progress state once at the top of get_comprehensive_data and derive level, power, names, thresholds and bars from that single snapshot; pass it into the helpers instead of letting each re-read.
findings.unsure_why: I cannot see mech_service.get_mech_state_service; if it itself reads progress_service.get_state() the disagreement needs a write between two reads a few milliseconds apart, which is rare.

findings.trigger: Two threads (waitress request threads plus the bot thread share the singleton) call get_comprehensive_data at the moment the 5-minute cleanup is due: thread A runs _cleanup_cache() iterating self._cache.items() while thread B executes _store_in_cache and inserts a new key -> 'RuntimeError: dictionary changed size during iteration', which get_comprehensive_data catches at line 363 and turns into MechDataResult(success=False, error='Runtime error: ...') - although the result had already been fully computed. Likewise two threads expiring the same key in _get_from_cache (line 845) -> KeyError -> caught at 356 -> success=False.
findings.suggestion: Guard _cache with a threading.Lock (or iterate over list(self._cache.items()) and use pop(key, None)); store the result before, not after, the cleanup so a cleanup failure cannot discard a computed result.
findings.unsure_why: Depends on whether the store is actually reached from more than one OS thread at once; the process model (one process, waitress threads + bot) suggests yes, but I cannot see the callers.

findings.trigger: Any exception in _calculate_progress_data (e.g. evo_max not numeric -> TypeError at line 731) -> returns progress_current=0, progress_max=20, progress_percentage=0.0 - fixed numbers nobody measured, delivered through get_power_info()/get_comprehensive_data() with success=True. The same function's comment (lines 720-723) states that 'not measured is None' and applies it three lines earlier for the next_threshold-is-None case, but the except branch still invents 0/20.
findings.suggestion: Return None for all three fields in the except branch, as the next_threshold-is-None branch already does.

findings.trigger: PowerDataRequest(include_decimals=False) or MechDataRequest(include_decimals=False) -> the flag lands in the cache key (line 262) but nothing in the calculation reads it: _get_core_mech_data always asks mech_service with include_decimals=True (line 538), and current_power is passed through unrounded. A caller asking for whole numbers receives 0.99 and pays for a second cache entry for the identical data.
findings.suggestion: Either round current_power/total_donated when include_decimals is False, or drop the field (and its cache-key part) and say so where the request is defined.
findings.unsure_why: Whether any caller passes include_decimals=False and displays the result unrounded is outside this section.

findings.trigger: (a) Operator's evolution.json gives level 2 a cost of 25 -> ceiling becomes 50/25 = 2.0; the panel slider allows 2.4 -> set_difficulty_multiplier(2.4) silently stores 2.0 and returns True ('saved'), the requested value is neither stored nor reported back. (b) The docstring promises 'the level-2 cost stays between LEVEL_2_COST_FLOOR and LEVEL_2_COST_CEILING', but calculate_dynamic_cost multiplies by the community multiplier afterwards (line 406-407): with a LARGE/MASSIVE tier multiplier of 1.5 the level-2 cost is 10 * 5.0 * 1.5 = 75 > 50. The clamp bounds only the difficulty share, not the cost.
findings.suggestion: Return or log the clamped value so the caller can show what was actually stored (or refuse out-of-range input); reword the docstring to 'the difficulty share of the level-2 cost' or include the community multiplier in the clamp.

findings.trigger: The event log already carries PowerGiftGranted for release_<version> but release_gifts_checked.json has no entry for <version> (the record write at line 207-209 failed with a WARNING at the first start, or the file was deleted/corrupt -> _release_decisions returns {}) -> restart on the same version: power_gift refuses with 'campaign already used', gift is None, and line 205-206 records the version as 'passed'. Two consequences: the next start logs 'the mech had energy at the first start of <version>', which is false; and when the admin later deletes that gift, the docstring's promise (lines 190-193: a deleted gift frees the campaign again) no longer holds, because line 197 short-circuits on 'passed' before the event-log check is ever reached.
findings.suggestion: Distinguish the three refusals: only record 'passed' when the refusal was 'power > 0'; when the campaign is already in the ledger record 'granted' (or nothing). Let power_gift return a reason, or check the ledger for the campaign before deciding the label.

findings.trigger: Snapshot lags behind the event log (a crash between append_event and persist_snapshot of a donation that levelled the mech up, the case _heal_if_lagging exists for) -> release_gift reads load_snapshot(...).level at line 201 BEFORE grant_power_gift heals at line 89, so the gift is sized as three_days_of_energy(old level) while the mech is already at the new level; the healed snapshot then receives a gift that is three days of the wrong level's consumption. The docstring's reason for holding the lock ('a donation that levels up in between would size the gift from the level the mech no longer has') is exactly this case, only with the stale snapshot instead of a concurrent donation.
findings.suggestion: Heal first: call service._heal_if_lagging(read_events()) in release_gift before load_snapshot, or let grant_power_gift accept a callable that sizes the gift from the healed snapshot.
findings.unsure_why: Needs a crash window between two writes; also I cannot see _heal_if_lagging and whether load_snapshot itself already folds pending events.

findings.trigger: Mech<N>/big/ contains walk frames but not exactly '<N>_walk_0001.png' (numbering starts at 0000, or the frame set is a subset) -> _has_big_version() says True (it globs '<N>_walk_*.png', line 132) while _get_size_ratio() returns 1.0 (line 153-154) without logging. get_mech_resolution_info() then reports success=True, has_big_version=True, size_ratio=1.0, cropping adjustments unscaled, and get_canvas_size_for_resolution(..., 'big') returns the SMALL canvas (270 x base) for an image 2.5-3x larger - a silently mis-cropped big mech.
findings.suggestion: Let both checks use the same file (e.g. the first walk frame the glob finds), and treat a missing pair as 'no big version' or as an error instead of ratio 1.0.
findings.unsure_why: Whether the shipped assets always contain _walk_0001.png is outside this section; with the shipped set the case may never occur.

findings.trigger: Dynamic costs in effect (difficulty multiplier 2.0, or a community multiplier != 1.0) and total donations of $15 -> get_evolution_level(15.0) compares against the BASE cost of level 2 ($10) and answers level 2, while the progress service (which applies calculate_dynamic_cost, $20) has the mech at level 1; get_evolution_info(15.0) then reports name, next_threshold, amount_needed and progress_to_next for the wrong level. mech_data_store.py:634-635 states this outright ('the level guessed from total donations is wrong with dynamic costs') yet these two public functions still offer it. Side effect: progress_to_next (line 316) divides by (next_threshold - current_threshold) and raises ZeroDivisionError when an operator gives two adjacent levels the same cost.
findings.suggestion: Either route both functions through the progress state / calculate_dynamic_cost, or mark them legacy and make sure no display path calls them; guard the division.
findings.unsure_why: Callers are outside this section; if only legacy/unused code calls get_evolution_level/get_evolution_info the wrong level is never shown.

notes: LOCK nesting: release_gift holds LOCK (line 194) and inside it calls service.get_state() and service.power_gift() -> grant_power_gift, which takes LOCK again (line 88). If LOCK were a plain threading.Lock this would deadlock on every start, so it is presumably an RLock - stated, not verified. | MechDataResult/LevelDataResult/... failure results carry plausible defaults (level 1, next_threshold 20.0, 'OFFLINE'); a caller that ignores 'success' shows a level-1 mech at $20 - by design of the pattern, but worth remembering when reading callers. | _calculate_evolution_data's failure branches put None into next_threshold/amount_needed, which then land in MechDataResult/EvolutionDataResult fields typed float; a caller formatting amount_needed with :.2f raises TypeError - the knock-on of review C24 for callers I cannot see. | _calculate_speed_data falls back to speed 0/'OFFLINE'/#888888 on any error - the same invented-value pattern as F3/F6, logged at ERROR; a mech with power shows as OFFLINE while the failure lasts. | EvolutionConfigService.save_config/_load_config rely on ConfigService._load_json_file/_save_json_file (private methods of another service; Z7 atomicity and cache invalidation after save cannot be judged here). reset_to_auto_difficulty writes 1.0 without the clamp set_difficulty_multiplier applies; with a level-2 base cost above 50 the 'auto' value is outside the clamp's own range. | get_evolution_level_info opens and parses decay.json on every call; mech_data_store calls it three times per cache miss and calculate_dynamic_cost once per level - performance only. | _get_cropping_adjustments has entries for levels 1-10 only; level 11 gets top/bottom 0 while get_canvas_size_for_resolution has a level-11 height - two tables that may have drifted, but I cannot tell whether the level-11 asset needs a crop. | get_evolution_level and get_evolution_info hard-code 11 levels; a config with more is ignored. | Fallback data gives level 2 a power_max of 10, lower than level 1's 20 - data, not code, but if power_max is the battery capacity a level-up from 1 to 2 with $15 of power would lose $5; progress_service is not in this section. | grant_power_gift: if current_power_cents can be negative (decay debt not settled), capacity - current_power exceeds the capacity and the ledger entry is larger than what 'fits' - depends on whether current_power_cents clamps at 0, which I cannot see. | _release_decisions keeps any string value, not only 'granted'/'passed'; harmless. | get_mech_data_store/get_evolution_config_service/get_mech_high_res_service create their singletons without a lock; a duplicate instance is harmless here.
